settings.title: Settings
settings.accountWhy: Keep your projects online as well as here, so they open on your other devices, and let Motiff Lab's server read sheet music and recordings for you.
settings.signInHow: No password: each time, a code comes to your email.
settings.scanWhat: Motiff Lab reads the notes from a PDF or photo of printed music, and writes down the notes it hears in an audio or video recording. It asks before each send.
settings.scanHowToRun: How to run your own server
settings.scanDocker: Run these with Docker in a copy of the Motiff Lab repository. The build takes a few minutes and downloads about 2 GB once; after that the server works offline.
settings.scanBadAddress: Give an address such as http://localhost:8765, with no path after it.
settings.scanConnected: Connected: the scan server runs {0}. Scanning is on.
settings.scanElsewhere: This address is another computer, so pages and recordings you send leave this one. Each send asks first.

transcribe.heading: Transcribe a recording
transcribe.setUp: Motiff Lab can write down the notes it hears in an audio or video recording of piano music, with the same scan server as scanning.
transcribe.setUpLink: Set up the scan server in Settings
transcribe.what: This browser takes the sound out of the recording, so a video's picture stays on this device, and sends the first 2½ minutes of sound to the scan server at {0}, which writes down the notes it hears and then deletes the sound. If this browser cannot read the file, the file itself is sent. The notes are a first draft, marked as detected for you to check by ear.
transcribe.sendHosted: Send the sound to Motiff Lab's scan server, which deletes it once heard
transcribe.sendElsewhere: Send the sound to {0}, which is another computer
transcribe.choose: Choose an audio or video recording to transcribe
transcribe.drop: Drop a recording here, or click to choose one
transcribe.busy: Listening… this takes a few seconds for each minute of sound
transcribe.heard: {0} s of the recording heard in {1} s, sending included.
transcribe.draft: Every note is marked as detected: it is what the engine heard, which misses the pedal and can mistake an overtone for a note. The bars assume 120 beats a minute, so they may not line up with the music yet.
transcribe.cut: Only the first 2½ minutes were heard. Transcribe a shorter passage to get the rest.
transcribe.tooLarge: This browser cannot take the sound out of this file, and the file is larger than the 50 MB that can be sent as it is.
transcribe.tooLargeTip: Record audio only, or a shorter passage: M4A or MP3 from a phone works well.
transcribe.notHeardTip: Record closer to the piano, with less noise around it.
transcribe.off: Transcription is off. Give the scan server's address in Settings.
transcribe.signIn: Sign in on Settings to transcribe with Motiff Lab's scan server.
transcribe.oldServer: This scan server cannot transcribe yet. Build and start it again from the latest Motiff Lab (see Settings).
transcribe.failed: The scan server could not transcribe this recording.
transcribe.tooLong: The scan server took too long to answer.
import.fileWhat: Motiff Lab reads MIDI (.mid) and MusicXML (.musicxml, .mxl) files up to 50 MB. The file is read in this browser and never leaves this device.
import.fileChoose: Choose a MIDI or MusicXML file
import.fileDrop: Drop a file here, or click to choose one
import.scanSetUp: Motiff Lab can read a PDF or a photo of printed music with a scan server.
import.scanWhat: A PDF of up to 8 pages, or a photo of one page, is sent to the scan server at {0} to be read, and deleted there as soon as it has been. A page takes 20 to 60 seconds. The notes come back marked as detected, for you to check.
import.scanWhatHere: A PDF of up to 8 pages, or a photo of one page, is sent to the scan server at {0} on this computer to be read, and deleted there as soon as it has been. A page takes 20 to 60 seconds. The notes come back marked as detected, for you to check.
import.scanSendElsewhere: Send the page to {0}, which is another computer
import.scanChoose: Choose a PDF or photo of printed music to scan
import.scanBusy: Reading the notes… this takes a while for each page
import.scanDrop: Drop a PDF or photo here, or click to choose one
import.scanTooLarge: This file is larger than 50 MB, the most the scan server reads.
import.scanTooLargeTip: Scan fewer pages at a time, or save the photo at a lower resolution.
import.scanNotReadTip: Try a sharper photo that shows the whole page, straight on and in good light.
import.goScan: Read the notes from it with Scan printed music
import.goRecording: Write down its notes with Notes from a recording
import.scanRead: {0} read in {1} s by the scan server.
import.scanFlagged: {0} of {1} may have been misread. Every note is marked as detected until you check it; after opening, the Scan tab in the workspace takes you to each of these bars.
import.scanClean: No bar looks wrong to the checks. The notes are still a reading of the page, marked as detected until you check them.
import.readHere: Read in {0} s on this device.
import.roundedHow: Rounded timing moves a note by at most half a tick, 1/960 of a quarter note.
import.notRounded: No timing had to be rounded.
import.noRestoreYet: Restore rhythm is not in this version yet, so for now the file plays as it was recorded.
import.warningKinds: Assumed: the file did not say, so Motiff Lab chose a value. Repaired: the file was damaged and Motiff Lab kept what it could read. Left out: not used in this version.
import.handsInferredWhy: Hands were worked out from pitch and movement, not read from the file.
import.openSaves: Opening saves the piece as a project, so you can come back to it.

understand.inScore: {0}, in the score and on the roll.
understand.offeredFor: A fact about the passage the experiment was offered for.
understand.legend: Detected: read from the notes or the file. Inferred: worked out by a rule. Uncertain: a guess on thin evidence. Basis shows why. Choose a fact that names places to see them in the score and on the roll.
understand.placeHint: Highlight only this place and move playback to its start.
